candidates.title: Predicting Operational Impact by Combining Formal Verifier Outputs with an Operational Simulator
candidates.research_question: Does combining deterministic verifier outputs with lightweight operational-simulator features improve prediction of high operational-impact events (outages, high rollback cost, long MTTR) compared with verifier outputs alone for LLM/agent-generated NetOps changes?
hypotheses: Combining verifier pass/fail signals and counterexample structure with simulator-derived operational features will yield higher discriminative performance (AUC-ROC) for predicting high-impact events than using verifier outputs alone.

Verifier outputs will correlate with functional metrics (reachability violations) but will have limited calibration for operational impact metrics (outage probability, rollback cost) without simulator features.

A simple logistic-regression baseline augmented with simulator features will achieve meaningful calibration improvements over verifier-only models, while more flexible models (random forest) will further increase discrimination but risk overfitting without careful cross-validation.
candidates.proposed_design: Preregister a corpus of synthetic and public multi-vendor configuration change tasks (intent-to-change pairs). For each candidate change: (1) generate an LLM/agent-produced configuration change using fixed prompts and model versions; (2) run a formal verifier (reachability/policy checks) to produce pass/fail and counterexample artifacts; (3) execute a deterministic operational simulator that estimates outage probability, simulated rollback cost, and MTTR under injected failure scenarios; (4) compute topology and traffic lightweight features (redundancy, affected prefix counts). Freeze seeds, models, verifier/tool versions, simulator parameters, and a maximum of 1,800 model calls. Split tasks into training/validation/test folds. Train predictive models (verifier-only features; verifier+simulator features) using nested cross-validation and report held-out metrics. Save all raw artifacts for reproducibility.
candidates.expected_data: Per-change records: verifier pass/fail, counterexample traces, simulator outage probability, estimated rollback cost, MTTR, topology/traffic features, model-generation logs. Aggregates: Pearson/Spearman correlations between verifier signals and operational metrics, AUC-ROC/AUPRC/Brier score for each model variant with 95% CIs, calibration curves, permutation feature importance and SHAP-like summaries, decision-curve analysis outputs.
candidates.primary_outcome: Increase in held-out AUC-ROC for predicting high operational-impact events when using verifier+simulator features versus verifier-only features, reported with 95% confidence intervals and p-value from a paired test across folds.
candidates.analysis_outline: Compute descriptive correlations between verifier outputs and continuous operational metrics. Train logistic regression and random-forest classifiers for binary high-impact prediction (predefined outage/rollback thresholds) with nested cross-validation. Report AUC-ROC, AUPRC, Brier score, and 95% CIs via bootstrap. Use paired Wilcoxon or paired t-tests across folds for primary outcome. Produce calibration plots and compute calibration-in-the-large and calibration slope. Compute permutation feature importance and SHAP summaries. Conduct sensitivity analyses varying simulator severity parameters and retraining to assess robustness.
risks: Operational simulator abstractions (traffic models, SLO thresholds) may misrepresent real-world operator priorities, limiting external validity.
Predictive models may overfit to simulated scenarios and not generalize to unseen topologies or traffic patterns.
Estimating rollback cost requires assumptions about change propagation and operator intervention that may be site-specific.

candidates.title: Audit of Data Contamination and Construct Validity in LLM-for-NetOps Benchmarks
candidates.research_question: How prevalent are dataset contamination and construct-invalidity issues in public LLM-for-NetOps benchmarks, and how much do contamination controls and realism adjustments affect measured model performance?
hypotheses: A nontrivial fraction of evaluated NetOps benchmark items will show probable overlap with public LLM training corpora according to exact-match and fuzzy-overlap heuristics, inflating measured performance.

Applying preregistered contamination controls (removing/holding out overlapping items and temporal splits) and realism adjustments (multi-vendor retemplating, added topology complexity) will produce a statistically significant decrease in measured model performance across evaluated benchmarks.

Tasks classified as highly templated or low-complexity will exhibit the largest performance drops after contamination control and realism adjustments, indicating construct-invalidity bias in published evaluations.
candidates.proposed_design: Select a representative set of public NetOps/LLM benchmarks and datasets from the literature leads. Preregister contamination-detection heuristics: exact fingerprint matching, fuzzy n-gram overlap thresholds, and metadata provenance tracing. For each dataset: (1) compute contamination flags; (2) create contamination-controlled splits by removing/holding out flagged items; (3) produce realism-adjusted variants (vendor retemplating, increased topology complexity). Evaluate a fixed set of LLMs and in-context prompting strategies on original vs controlled/realistic splits using identical prompts and scoring. Limit model calls to 1,200. Record provenance traces for flagged items and all evaluation logs.
candidates.expected_data: Per-dataset contamination rates (counts and percentages), model performance on original vs controlled splits (accuracy, repair rate), per-task performance deltas, distribution of contamination across sources, and classification of tasks by construct-validity (templated vs realistic). Aggregates: mean performance drop with 95% CIs and sensitivity curves across contamination thresholds.
candidates.primary_outcome: Average relative drop in model performance (percentage points) across evaluated benchmarks after applying preregistered contamination controls and realism adjustments, with 95% confidence intervals and task-level variance estimates.
candidates.analysis_outline: Report contamination prevalence descriptively. Use paired comparisons (paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank) of per-task model scores original vs cleaned splits. Compute effect sizes (Cohen’s d or equivalent). Stratify results by task construct categories and perform sensitivity analyses across contamination-detection thresholds. Document provenance traces and estimate false-positive/false-negative rates for heuristics using manual spot checks on random samples.
risks: Contamination-detection heuristics can produce false positives/negatives; overly aggressive cleaning may remove valid evaluation items.
Access to authoritative LLM training-corpus manifests is limited, so overlap inferences remain probabilistic.
Audit results are potentially sensitive for dataset maintainers and require careful non-defamatory reporting and responsible disclosure.

candidates.title: Safety Evaluation of Agentic NetOps Repair Systems under Adversarial and Multi-Agent Interactions
candidates.research_question: How do agentic NetOps repair systems combining LLMs, retrieval, and formal verifiers behave under adversarial input perturbations and emergent multi-agent interactions, and which failure modes are most likely to lead to unsafe operational outcomes?
hypotheses: Agentic systems that include retrieval and verifier steps will outperform naive LLM-only repair on benign scenarios but will still be vulnerable to targeted adversarial prompt/intent perturbations that induce unsafe repairs.

Emergent multi-agent interactions (conflicting agent goals or chained autonomous changes) will increase the frequency of regressions and increase outage probability relative to single-agent baselines.

Specific failure modes (retrieval poisoning, verifier-bypass via crafted outputs, and conflicting change sequences) will account for a majority of high-impact adverse events observed in adversarial scenarios.
candidates.proposed_design: Construct a suite of NetOps repair tasks with benign misconfigurations and adversarial variants (crafted prompts, poisoned retrieval context, and chained multi-agent change sequences). Implement an agentic repair pipeline (LLM generation + retrieval + verifier + iterative repair loop) and a baseline LLM-only repair pipeline. Define adversarial attack types and severity levels, and preregister attack generation heuristics and budgets. For multi-agent experiments, simulate multiple agents issuing sequential or conflicting changes under timing schedules. Run verifiers and an operational simulator to measure outages/rollback/MTTR. Limit model calls to 2,000. Log all interactions, retrieval contexts, verifier traces, and agent message transcripts.
candidates.expected_data: Per-task and per-attack records: repair proposals, retrieval context snapshots, verifier results and counterexamples, simulator outage probability, rollback cost, MTTR, and timelines of multi-agent interactions. Aggregates: attack success rates, relative regression rates vs baselines, breakdown of failure modes, and per-attack impact distributions.
candidates.primary_outcome: Increase in regression/unsafe-event rate (and operational impact metrics) for agentic and LLM-only pipelines under adversarial perturbations and multi-agent interactions versus benign baselines, reported with 95% CIs and attack-type stratification.
candidates.analysis_outline: Compute attack success rates and compare pipelines using paired statistical tests. Estimate relative risk ratios for unsafe events under each attack class. Use survival-style analysis for time-to-recovery (MTTR) across scenarios. Produce confusion-matrix-style breakdowns of observed failure modes and attribute impact via manual and automated clustering of verifier counterexamples. Perform ablation studies disabling retrieval or verifier components to measure their protective effects.
risks: Designing realistic adversarial scenarios risks producing unrealistic worst-case attacks that overstate real-world prevalence.
Simulated multi-agent interactions may not capture human operator mitigation behaviors, reducing external validity.
Ethical disclosure of adversarial vulnerabilities must avoid actionable guidance that could be misused; responsible disclosure procedures are required.

candidates.title: Design and Pilot of an Oracle-Backed Multi-Vendor NetOps Benchmark Linking Functional Verification to Operational Impact
candidates.research_question: Can a standardized pilot benchmark that couples multi-vendor configuration corpora, realistic topologies, formal verification oracles, and simulated operational-impact metrics provide reproducible, auditable evaluation of LLM/agentic NetOps methods and reveal gaps between functional correctness and operational risk?
hypotheses: An oracle-backed benchmark combining formal verifier outputs with operational-simulator metrics will expose cases where verifier-passed changes still produce non-negligible operational risk (outage probability, rollback cost).
LLM and agentic methods that optimize for verifier pass rate alone will underperform methods that explicitly optimize or gate on combined operational-impact metrics when measured under the benchmark.

A compact, well-documented pilot benchmark (public topologies, templated multi-vendor configs, verifier contracts) will be feasible to run reproducibly and will enable clearer nearest-work comparisons than existing fragmented suites.
candidates.proposed_design: Create a pilot benchmark repository containing: (1) a small set of public realistic topologies and synthesized multi-vendor configuration corpora; (2) a formal verifier integration (reachability and policy oracles) with standardized input/output contracts; (3) an operational simulator for outage/rollback/MTTR estimation; and (4) a task suite (intent-to-change, misconfiguration repair, and policy update). Define evaluation metrics that include functional pass rates and operational-impact measures. Pilot the benchmark by evaluating several public LLMs and a simple agentic pipeline, recording all artifacts and a reproducible setup. Preregister dataset construction procedures, template sources, and oracle semantics. Limit model calls to 1,500 for the pilot.
candidates.expected_data: Benchmark artifacts: topology and config corpora, verifier logs, simulator outputs per task (outage prob, rollback cost, MTTR), per-model scores (functional and operational metrics), and reproducibility manifests. Aggregates: task-level discrepancies between verifier pass rates and operational-impact measurements, per-method rankings under combined metrics, and benchmark reproducibility checksums.
candidates.primary_outcome: Measured prevalence of tasks where verifier pass does not imply low operational risk (percentage of verifier-pass cases with nontrivial outage probability or rollback cost) in the pilot benchmark, with 95% CIs.
candidates.analysis_outline: Report descriptive statistics on verifier pass vs operational-impact distributions. Compute conditional probabilities P(high-risk | verifier-pass). Compare method rankings under functional-only metrics vs combined operational metrics using rank-correlation measures (Spearman rho). Evaluate reproducibility by re-running a subset and comparing checksums and result variance. Provide example case studies illustrating divergence between verifier signals and operational impact.
risks: Creating multi-vendor realistic config corpora risks inadvertent inclusion of sensitive templates; use only public or synthesized sources.
Pilot benchmark simulator and oracle abstractions may not generalize to all operator SLOs; users must treat metrics as indicative rather than definitive.
Maintaining reproducibility requires careful artifact hashing and hosting; broken links or changed external resources can degrade long-term reproducibility.
